Beginning with the 2024 assessments, the National Assessment of Educational Progress (NAEP) reports results by a **socioeconomic status (SES) index** built from student and school information. This report uses the [NAEP Data Service API](https://www.nationsreportcard.gov/api_documentation.aspx) to show how achievement varies by SES within each of the `r n_tuda` large urban districts that took part in the 2024 [Trial Urban District Assessment](https://nces.ed.gov/nationsreportcard/tuda/).

::: {.callout-note appearance="simple"}
## At a glance (grade 8 mathematics)

- In large cities, `r low_share("Large city", "Mathematics", 8)`% of eighth-graders are in the Low SES group, compared with `r low_share("National public", "Mathematics", 8)`% in the nation's public schools.
- High SES eighth-graders in large cities scored `r ref_gap("Large city", "Mathematics", 8)` points higher in mathematics than their Low SES peers (national public: `r ref_gap("National public", "Mathematics", 8)` points).
- Across districts with reportable results, that gap ranges from `r gap_range("Mathematics", 8)[1]` to `r gap_range("Mathematics", 8)[2]` points.
- On the 9-point (3-component) SES index scale, large-city eighth-graders with the highest index score (9) averaged `r point_mean("Large city", "Mathematics", 8, 9)` in mathematics, `r point_gap("Large city", "Mathematics", 8)` points above those with the lowest score (0) (national public: `r point_gap("National public", "Mathematics", 8)` points).
:::

## Average scores by SES level

Each row is a district; dots show the average scale score of its Low, Middle, and High SES students. Districts are sorted by the Low SES average. **National public** and **Large city** are shown in bold for reference. Hover over a dot for the score and the share of the district's students in that SES group. Missing dots mean NAEP did not report the estimate because reporting standards were not met.

::: panel-tabset

## Results by SES index score

The Low, Middle, and High SES groups above are built from an underlying **SES index score**. NAEP also reports results at each point of the index. This section uses the 3-component index (0 to 9) at both grades, so grade 8 results here use a different index than the 4-component (12-point) index behind the grade 8 SES groups above. Higher scores mean higher SES. The point scale shows how achievement changes across the full SES range rather than across three broad groups.

### Average scores by SES index score

Each cell is the average scale score of a district's students at one SES index score. Darker cells mean higher scores. Districts are sorted by their overall average score, with the highest at the top. Blank cells are estimates NAEP did not report, which happens most often at the ends of the scale where few students are found. Hover over a cell to see the score and the share of the district's students at that index score.

::: panel-tabset

## About the data

**Source.** U.S. Department of Education, NCES, National Assessment of Educational Progress (NAEP), 2024 Mathematics and Reading Assessments, retrieved from the NAEP Data Service API (`GetAdhocData`). Data use the `SESCAT` variable (SES index, 3 components, categorized) for grade 4 and the `SESCATP` variable (SES index, 4 components, categorized) for grade 8, and the point-scale 3-component index, `SESCMP` (scores 0–9), at both grades, with `MN:MN` (average score), `RP:RP` (percent of students), `ALC:AB` and `ALC:AP` (percent at or above Basic and Proficient).

**The NAEP SES index.** Grade 4 results use the 3-component index (9-point scale), which combines the student's economically disadvantaged status, the percentage of students in the student's school classified as economically disadvantaged, and the number of books in the student's home (student-reported). Grade 8 results use the 4-component index (12-point scale), which adds the highest level of parental education (student-reported); it is available only at grades 8 and 12. Because the two grades use different versions of the index, SES group results are not directly comparable across grades. NAEP groups index scores into Low, Middle, and High SES; the point-scale results report each index score separately and use the 3-component index at both grades. (On NAEP data files the point-scale variable is named `SES3VAL`; the API calls it `SESCMP`.) For more on how the index is built and used, see the [NAEP SES Index dashboard](https://www.nationsreportcard.gov/dashboards/sesindex/) and the [Focus on NAEP article on the SES index](https://www.nationsreportcard.gov/focus_on_naep/articles/#/ses).

**Districts.** The 26 TUDA districts assessed in 2024 are compared with **National public** (all public schools in the nation) and **Large city** (public schools in cities with populations of 250,000 or more).

**Caveats.**

- *Suppressed estimates.* Where NAEP reporting standards were not met, estimates are shown as missing. High SES results are suppressed in several districts, and Denver has no reportable SES results in 2024.
- *No significance testing.* The API returns point estimates without standard errors, so differences shown here have not been tested for statistical significance. Use the [NAEP Data Explorer](https://www.nationsreportcard.gov/ndecore/xplore/NDE) for that.
- *Scale comparisons.* Mathematics and reading are on separate scales, and grade 4 and grade 8 results are not directly comparable.
